subject: Re: DPA and transfer-routing questions for Redwood platform (RoyalCare)
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@royalcare.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@royalcare.com>, contracts@rowanllp.com
Date: 2026-09-10T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: DPA + transfer routing questions for Redwood platform

Hi Michael / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — RoyalCare is interested in moving forward but we need clarity on a few DPA/transfer items before procurement can push the SOW through. Quick list of asks to help our legal and security teams:

1) Which transfer mechanism do you anticipate for EU->US processing? Are you offering SCCs + UK Addendum / IDTA by default, or do we need a DTIA with mitigations?
2) Subprocessor list: can you supply a current CSV and flag any planned additions for the next 90 days (we recently had a reserve for edge cache providers).
3) Technical evidence: we need a short TIA artifact set that covers network residency controls (edge caching, prefix caching), encryption (at-rest/in-transit), and KMS/HSM details.
4) For Dedicated/Private placements: can you confirm whether data can be constrained to a UK region and what the operational handoff looks like?
5) Timeline: we need to sign a DPA + Transfer Annex within the month to hit our procurement window.

Attaching our procurement checklist — please point us to the matching artifacts or a timeline for delivery.

Appreciate a short call if that helps.

Best,
Alice Morgan
Head of Procurement, RoyalCare Health Systems
alice.morgan@royalcare.com
(415) 555-0112

Attachment: royalcare_procurement_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: michael.grant@redwood.com <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@royalcare.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + transfer routing questions for Redwood platform

Alice — thanks, and great to hear the team wants to proceed. High-level answers here and then I’ll loop in Legal for redlines. Short answers first:

- Transfer mechanism: We support EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and we can execute the UK Addendum / UK IDTA where the customer requires it. For customers with elevated risk we also run a DTIA/DTIA-plus and add compensating controls.
- Subprocessors: I’ve exported the current list and included it as a CSV. We’ll flag any scheduled additions for the next 90 days.
- Technical evidence: our Security team has a TIA evidence packet that includes: network residency maps, caching behaviour (prefix/KV), TLS configs, and KMS/HSM summary. I’ll attach the summary PDF and can share a longer pack under NDA if needed.
- Dedicated/Private: Yes — Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in a UK-only tenancy; we can provide network diagrams and enclave handoff procedures.

Next concrete steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to review and produce a DPA redline and confirm whether we can commit to the UK IDTA language as-is or need some limited carveouts.
2) Security to prepare the TIA-evidence-summary (I’m attaching an initial draft).
3) Set a 30-minute call with RoyalCare legal and procurement for Tuesday to align cadence.

We can hit the month timeline if we prioritize the DPA redline + evidence handoff this week.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Director, Compliance & Trust, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
(650) 555-2040

Attachments: pipeline_subprocessor_list.csv, TIA-evidence-summary.pdf

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@royalcare.com>, michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, contracts@rowanllp.com
Date: 2026-09-11T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + transfer routing questions for Redwood platform

Alice / team — I reviewed the procurement checklist and Michael’s notes. I’ve attached a redline (RoyalCare_DPA_redline_v2.docx) with comments on the transfer annex. To summarize our positions and open items: 

- UK IDTA: We can sign the UK Addendum (IDTA) in combination with SCCs where RoyalCare requires UK-specific safeguards. We cannot agree to unconditional onshore guarantees for third-party subprocessor caches; instead we propose a contractual residency commitment for primary model data + the fallback policy enumerated in the redline.

- DTIA/TIAs: Please confirm whether RoyalCare accepts a DTIA with compensating technical controls for edge caching. If you require a full prescriptive _on-prem_ proof, we can offer a Private deployment package but that’s a separate commercial engagement.

- Evidence list needed from Redwood for your reviewers (I marked required vs optional):
  * Required: current subprocessor csv (with role, region), KMS provider(s) + HSM attestation summary, TLS matrix (versions/ciphers), network flow diagram showing where KV/prefix caching can occur.
  * Optional: perf/latency benchmarks by region, transfer audit log samples (redacted).

- Subprocessor flags: highlight any subprocessor that performs caching or request-level routing (e.g., CDN/edge cache, smart proxy). We need that to assess residual risk.

If RoyalCare is okay to accept the redline + a DTIA with our compensating controls we can proceed to DocuSign and aim to finish signature within ~10 business days after evidence handoff. I’ve included inline comments in the doc where we request confirmatory language (e.g., definition of "personal data" scope, logging retention).

Michael — can you confirm the expected delivery date for the full subprocessor CSV and the HSM attestation? Rishi / Laura — please review the DocuSign envelope in the link and flag any nonstandard clauses.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: RoyalCare_DPA_redline_v2.docx (redline stub)
Related link: https://www.docusign.com/embedded?envelopeId=abc-rc-2026

From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@royalcare.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@royalcare.com>, laura.bennett@royalcare.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, contracts@rowanllp.com
Date: 2026-09-12T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + transfer routing questions for Redwood platform

Kim / Michael — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. A few responses and requests inline: 

> "We can sign the UK Addendum (IDTA) in combination with SCCs where RoyalCare requires UK-specific safeguards."

Understood — RoyalCare prefers the UK Addendum + SCCs for PHI-adjacent workloads. Please mark the DPA redline where the Addendum text will be inserted and confirm whether any residual carveouts remain (e.g., for performance caching).

> "We cannot agree to unconditional onshore guarantees for third-party subprocessor caches; instead we propose a contractual residency commitment for primary model data + the fallback policy..."

Noted. Can you provide a short summary table that maps which types of requests/data may be cached at the edge and which are never cached (we need that for our security review).

> Evidence delivery / timeline

We accept the DTIA approach with compensating controls if Redwood provides the required artifacts within 5 business days (subprocessor CSV + HSM attestation + network flow diagram). That gives us time to review and proceed to signature. If you can hit that window we’ll route the DPA for signature the following week.

We also have one flagged subprocessor: EdgeCache Inc. — please call that out and provide whether they perform any unredacted logging of content or full-text storage.

Call: we can do a short 30-minute alignment call on Monday 09/14 11:00am UK time — does that work for your team?

Appreciate it,
Alice Morgan
Head of Procurement, RoyalCare Health Systems
